description: Calculate CSS selector specificity as (a,b,c) with a full breakdown — handles IDs, classes, attributes, pseudo-classes, :not(), :is(), :where() and pseudo-elements.

faqs.a: Count ID selectors (#), then classes/attributes/pseudo-classes (.), then elements/pseudo-elements — written as (a,b,c). A higher component always beats lower ones combined.
:not(), :is() and :has() take the specificity of their most specific argument; :where() always contributes 0.
No — (0,1,0) beats (0,0,11): a single class outranks any number of elements. Compare component by component.
Yes, everything runs locally in your browser.
